title: Natural language processing
blurb: From term weighting and n-gram models to word vectors, sequence-to-sequence models and pretraining, then retrieval and speech recognition.

main.title: Stanford CS224N: Natural Language Processing with Deep Learning
main.why: Word vectors, parsing, language models, translation, Transformers and pretraining. In English.

main.title: Term Weighting Approaches in Automatic Text Retrieval
main.why: TF-IDF. Weight each term by its count in the document and its rarity in the collection, then normalize for length.

main.title: Simple, Proven Approaches to Text Retrieval
main.why: BM25. Combines IDF, term frequency and document length into the formula Elasticsearch still uses by default.

main.title: Two Decades of Statistical Language Modeling: Where Do We Go from Here?
main.why: N-gram language models. Perplexity, smoothing, and the extensions that tried to fix their weaknesses.

main.title: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model
main.why: Neural language model. Learned word vectors let it beat smoothed n-gram models.
word2vec. Skip-gram and CBOW, cheap enough to train on billions of words.

further.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation

main.title: Sequence to Sequence Learning with Neural Networks
main.why: Seq2seq. One LSTM encodes the source sentence and another decodes the translation.

main.title: Neural Machine Translation by Jointly Learning to Align and Translate
main.why: Attention. The decoder searches the source sentence at every step instead of relying on one fixed vector.

main.title: Neural Machine Translation of Rare Words with Subword Units
main.why: BPE. Rare words become sequences of frequent subword units, so a fixed vocabulary can translate any word.

main.title: Improving Language Understanding by Generative Pre-Training
main.why: GPT. Pretrain a Transformer decoder on unlabeled text, then fine-tune it for each task.
BERT. Predicting masked words pretrains an encoder that reads in both directions.

further.title: RoBERTa: A Robustly Optimized BERT Pretraining Approach
DistilBERT, a Distilled Version of BERT: Smaller, Faster, Cheaper and Lighter
Unsupervised Cross-lingual Representation Learning at Scale
DeBERTa: Decoding-enhanced BERT with Disentangled Attention
Smarter, Better, Faster, Longer: A Modern Bidirectional Encoder for Fast, Memory Efficient, and Long Context Finetuning and Inference

main.title: Language Models are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
main.why: GPT-2. A 1.5B-parameter language model trained on WebText handles many tasks zero-shot, with no fine-tuning.

main.title: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer
main.why: T5. Every task becomes text in, text out, and pretraining choices are compared one at a time.

main.title: Sentence-BERT: Sentence Embeddings using Siamese BERT-Networks
main.why: Sentence-BERT. Sentence embeddings compared by cosine turn a 65-hour similarity search into 5 seconds.

main.title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
main.why: DPR. A dual encoder trained on question-passage pairs beats BM25 at retrieval.

main.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
main.why: RAG. BART writes answers from Wikipedia passages that DPR retrieves, so knowledge sits in a swappable index.
Podcast search moves from term matching to a fine-tuned multilingual sentence encoder.

main.title: Connectionist Temporal Classification: Labelling Unsegmented Sequence Data with Recurrent Neural Networks
main.why: CTC. Trains a recognizer on audio and transcripts with no frame-by-frame alignment.

main.title: wav2vec 2.0: A Framework for Self-Supervised Learning of Speech Representations
main.why: wav2vec 2.0. Pretrain on unlabeled audio, then fine-tune on as little as ten minutes of transcribed speech.
Whisper. 680,000 hours of web audio with transcripts give robust recognition with no fine-tuning.
